summary: Redwood AE + SE reviewed SSO/SAML SSO flow, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC least-privilege design with ConsumerCloud security and infra. Customer requested SCIM attribute mapping examples, RBAC role spreadsheet, and SOC2 artifacts. Agreement to run a follow-up runbook workshop and share docs.
transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-03-25 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Marcus Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alex Gomez (Head of Security, ConsumerCloud), Priya Patel (Director IT), Samir Rao (SRE Lead), Lena Ortiz (Legal)

00:00 Marcus: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Marcus from Redwood, i'll hand over to Priya N for the deep dive on SSO and RBAC.
00:08 Priya N: hi all, thanks, quick agenda: we'll run through SAML metadata exchange, SCIM provisioning flow, then RBAC/least-privilege model and then time for q&a. if there's anything urgent flag it.
00:22 Alex: great, we have about 50 minutes, short intro: i'm alex, i look after sec. our main asks: we need SAML SSO with Okta, SCIM for provisioning groups, fine-grained RBAC, and audit logs export to our splunk. also need KMS customer-managed keys for encrypting data at rest.
00:38 Marcus: noted, thanks. couple quick qual questions: are you using Okta as IdP now for all apps?
00:42 Alex: yes, okta is primary. we also have some legacy on-prem ad for a handful of service accounts.
00:48 Priya N: cool, SCIM support for Okta is standard; we'll show attribute mapping. quick note, our SCIM implementation uses the canonical urn for groups and supports incremental syncs, though sometimes the attr names differ, sorry i'll show an example.
01:05 Samir: question — for SCIM do you support group-to-role mapping or do we have to map groups client-side?
01:10 Priya N: good q. Redwood supports group-to-role mappings server-side via SCIM group membership -> RBAC binding. we can either accept group external IDs and map to roles, or you can push an explicit role attribute. in practice we usually do group mapping in the provisioning layer.
01:28 Priya P: any auto-provisioning constraints for service accounts? we prefer manual for service accounts.
01:33 Priya N: yep we can exclude certain user filters in the SCIM filters, e.g., filter by userType or custom attr not to provision.
01:45 Alex: on RBAC, we want least privilege. what are the builtin roles vs custom roles?
01:49 Priya N: we have a few managed roles: Admin, Operator, Viewer, and Billing. but we recommend you create custom roles — our console supports granular permissions, e.g., route.create, model.deploy, key.view (limited), audit.read. we can provide a role template sheet.
02:08 Marcus: and to be clear about key.view — by default Redwood does not expose plaintext keys; KMS integration handles key material.
02:16 Lena: question from legal — do you have contractual language for data residency and audit log access, and what's the retention policy for logs?
02:25 Marcus: we do, i'll send the SOC 2/ISO whitepaper and our log-retention options. default is 90 days in hosted but we have enterprise add-ons for longer retention and S3 log export.
02:38 Alex: we'd like logs forwarded to our Splunk and also have tamper-evident storage.
02:45 Priya N: we support syslog/HTTP push to external collectors and S3 bucket exports; tamper evidence usually via object versioning + signed manifests. note: some customers also use AWS KMS with customer-managed keys to encrypt logs at rest.
03:05 Samir: for KMS do you support customer-managed keys (CMKs) in our AWS account? or do you require Redwood-managed keys?
03:12 Priya N: we support both. for private deployments we recommend customer KMS in your VPC; for hosted we can do external encryption via AWS KMS grants for S3 export or bring-your-own-key (BYOK) flows. there are some HSM/KMS integration steps we'll share.
03:34 Alex: what about SCIM attribute fidelity — are custom attributes preserved (e.g., manager, department)?
03:40 Priya N: yes most custom attributes are preserved if mapped; there are occasionally naming mismatches — like sometimes 'department' comes in as 'dept' from the IdP — we'll include an example mapping and troubleshooting tips.
03:58 Marcus: wanted to flag we've had a couple transcriptions in the docs where product names were garbled — so in the doc we'll use explicit XML and JSON samples.
04:10 Priya P: on SAML, can you support Just-In-Time (JIT) provisioning?
04:15 Priya N: yes JIT for SAML is supported but we strongly prefer SCIM for full lifecycle — JIT is fine for initial sign-on but doesn't handle deprovisioning or group sync reliably.
04:30 Alex: deprovisioning is a hard req for us because of least-privilege and compliance.
04:35 Priya N: understoood; SCIM deprovisioning with delta sync is the recommended flow.
04:46 Samir: operational question — how do you handle session timeout and SSO session revocation when we disable a user in Okta?
04:52 Priya N: sessions honor the IdP session and we offer short-lived tokens; we also expose an API endpoint to revoke sessions and force logout. SCIM delta will remove membership and you can call revoke endpoint as part of your offboarding script.
05:12 Alex: legal question — do you produce audit evidence for SOC 2 re: access control changes?
05:18 Marcus: yes we have admin audit logs for role changes, user provisioning, and API key issuance. we can produce an export for auditors. retention and export cadence is part of enterprise contract.
05:35 Lena: please note we need a log export demonstrating role changes for the last 12 months as an example in our RFP.
05:42 Marcus: we'll include a sample export and details on retention tiers.
05:48 Priya N: quick demo now — show SAML metadata exchange sample. (screen share noises) 
06:12 Priya N: so here's the IdP metadata XML, you'll upload it to Okta and map the assertion consumer service URL etc. our default NameID is email but we can configure username or persistent id.
06:32 Alex: does Redwood support Encrypted Assertions? some of our apps require them.
06:36 Priya N: Encrypted Assertions are supported but note there are additional key exchange steps; we'll include that in the doc.
06:50 Samir: what about SCIM rate limits and bulk provisioning?
06:55 Priya N: SCIM rate limits exist on hosted to protect multitenant runtime; typical is 10 req/s with burst capacity for provisioning. for large migrations we recommend a bulk provisioning job or using our onboarding API which has higher quotas for one-time jobs.
07:20 Alex: okay good. can you show how group to role mapping looks?
07:24 Priya N: yes, example: okta group externalId 'eng-platform' -> role 'Operator' in Redwood. we map group attribute 'members' to user ids and apply the mapping. we'll provide a CSV mapping template.
07:45 Priya P: about PRs and branches — unrelated but curious: how do you handle developer access to the prod console?
07:52 Marcus: choose least privilege; typically we grant developers Viewer or Operator on a per-route basis; only a handful of SREs and security folks are Admin.
08:06 Samir: we want to use SSO for console, but still allow service accounts for CI. how do you secure service account keys?
08:12 Priya N: service account keys are long-lived tokens; we recommend short-lived ephemeral tokens via our internal token broker or rotating keys and restricting scopes. keys are stored encrypted with KMS and visible only to Admins.
08:30 Alex: do you provide automatic key rotation?
08:34 Priya N: yes for private deployments we can automate rotation; hosted we have rotation APIs and we can help with a rotation schedule.
08:45 Lena: any PCI or HIPAA related controls relevant? consumer data is PII but not PHI; however our contracts require some HIPAA-adjacent safeguards.
08:56 Marcus: we have a compliance pack; for HIPAA adjacent controls we can provide a BAA and relevant safeguards — we'll follow up offline.
09:08 Alex: question around RBAC scoping: can roles be scoped to an org, a project, or route-level?
09:14 Priya N: yes roles are hierarchical: account-level, project-level and route/model-level. you can bind a role to a team or a specific model route. this helps with least privilege so devs get only the routes they need.
09:35 Samir: can we have user-level allow/deny overrides?
09:38 Priya N: we support explicit denies at the role level but recommend using narrow allow permissions with separate admin roles; explicit deny is a bit trickier and we generally discourage complex deny lists as they can become hard to reason about.
09:55 Alex: about audit logs — can Redwood redact sensitive fields before exporting? we have to avoid leaking some PII in logs.
10:02 Priya N: yes we support log redaction rules; you can configure patterns to redact PII before logs are sent to external systems. redaction happens pre-export to Splunk/S3.
10:18 Marcus: want to call attention to a common misnomer — KV cache sometimes shows up as KV 'cash' in transcripts, so for performance docs see our caching guide.
10:30 Samir: performance question — will RBAC checks add latency to inference calls?
10:36 Priya N: RBAC is enforced at the control plane and route admission time; per-token path doesn't incur extra latency on the serving runtime. there is a tiny auth check on each request but it's cached per session.
10:50 Alex: are role changes eventually consistent? we need deterministic enforcement for compliance.
10:55 Priya N: role changes are propagated via our control plane; enforcement is near-real-time (sub-minute) but for absolute compliance we recommend revoking active sessions via the revoke API which ensures immediate effect.
11:12 Lena: on data residency — some of our data must remain in the EU. how does Redwood support region-specific hosting?
11:19 Marcus: Redwood has region tagging and can pin model routes to EU regions; for full data residency we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment in the desired region. hosted EU regions store logs and data in EU only if configured.
11:35 Alex: cost question — does using CMK or extra log retention add cost?
11:39 Marcus: yes CMK and longer retention are add-ons; we'll include pricing in the follow-up.
11:50 Priya N: quick show of SCIM mapping UI — (screen noises) here you can map Okta attributes to Redwood user schema, exclude filters, and set provisioning rules.
12:12 Samir: do you support on-prem connector for SCIM if our Okta is behind VPN?
12:18 Priya N: we have a connector pattern for hybrid IdP setups; for very restricted environments we recommend a Private deployment.
12:30 Alex: are there known gotchas with Azure AD vs Okta?
12:34 Priya N: Azure AD has slightly different SCIM attribute names and some restrictions on group membership pagination; we'll include specific notes.
12:50 Marcus: let's cover the RBAC spreadsheet we promised — we usually provide a template mapping common IdP groups to Redwood roles; that helps your security team review least-privilege.
13:05 Priya P: would be great to get that template with exact permission names.
13:09 Priya N: yes we'll export a CSV with permission slugs like 'route.deploy', 'model.rollback', etc.
13:25 Alex: any concerns about SAML 2.0 assertions size? we have bigger assertions in some legacy apps.
13:30 Priya N: our SAML consumer supports larger assertion sizes but some IdPs truncate attributes; test with your Okta instance, we'll help debug.
13:45 Samir: for audit trail integrity do you provide signing of log exports?
13:49 Priya N: yes exports can be signed and checksummed; combined with S3 object versioning this supports tamper-evidence.
14:05 Marcus: ok let's surface the must-have asks: SCIM attribute map, RBAC template, SOC2 artifacts, KMS integration steps, and a runbook for user offboarding.
14:18 Alex: agreed. also can you include an example auditor query for role change events?
14:23 Marcus: yes we'll add an example Splunk query and event format.
14:30 Lena: one more legal ask — sample DPAs and data processing boundary language.
14:35 Marcus: we'll include DPA snippets and point to our legal team for negotiation.
14:42 Priya N: any other technical blockers?
14:44 Samir: one more, do you log API calls that contain prompts? there are privacy concerns around prompt storage.
14:50 Priya N: by default request payloads are logged minimally for debugging but we have redaction policies; for sensitive workloads we recommend private deployments with customer-managed KMS and to enable request redaction. we'll detail that.
15:05 Alex: perfect. let's recap next steps.
15:09 Marcus: recap: Marcus send SSO/SAML guide, Priya send RBAC spreadsheet and SCIM template, schedule runbook workshop 2026-04-01, customer to send current Okta group list.
15:24 Alex: sounds good. thanks everyone.
15:28 Marcus: thanks, we'll follow up via email with the docs.

(End of meeting)

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels (Priya vs Priya P), small mis-hearings (KV cash / kv cache), some product names abbreviated.

Attachments referenced: SSO_SAML_metadata_example.xml, SCIM_mapping_template.csv, RBAC_role_template.csv, SOC2_whitepaper.pdf, KMS_integration_steps.md
